newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower Tuesday in line with LME copper prices, after a sharp fall Monday on profit taking, with rumors of Chinese copper sales in the market.
But overnight Chinese officials denied any immediate plans to sell copper from the central reserve bureau's stockpile.

Meanwhile, workers at Inco Ltd's in Ontario, Canada, went on strike at the company's nickel and copper mine at Sudbury and the refinery in Port Colborne. The Ontario division produces about 200 million lbs of copper a year.
COMEX July copper was called 0.20 to 0.50 cent lower from Monday's close of 117.15 cents a lb as the market corrects from last week's eight-month high for nearby copper futures.
LME warehouse copper stocks fell a further 525 tonnes to 132,500 tonnes in Tuesday's data, while COMEX copper stocks fell 341 short tons Monday to 42,632 short tons.
